---
title: "Algorithms use the amsthm definition style"
format:
  latex: default
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
    theorem-appearance: fancy
_quarto:
  tests:
    latex:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        -
          - '\\theoremstyle\{definition\}\s*\\newtheorem\{algorithm\}'
        -
          - '\\theoremstyle\{plain\}\s*\\newtheorem\{algorithm\}'
    typst:
      ensureTypstFileRegexMatches:
        -
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"algorithm",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){4}\s*get-border-color: get-primary-border-color,'
        -
          - 'make-frame\((\r\n?|\n)\s*"algorithm",(\r\n?|\n)(.*(\r\n?|\n)){4}\s*get-border-color: get-secondary-border-color,'
---

The amsthm documentation lists algorithms with definitions, examples and
exercises in the `definition` style, so their body is upright in LaTeX output.
In the Typst `fancy` appearance, algorithms use the primary colour set, as
the other `definition`-style blocks do.

::: {#alg-a}
An algorithm.
:::
